question: In 2020, five big speech-recognition systems transcribed Black and white American speakers. How did their error rates compare?
options: Ten times higher for Black speakers
answer: Nearly double for Black speakers. Across systems from Amazon, Apple, Google, IBM and Microsoft, about 35 words in 100 came out wrong for Black speakers, against 19 for white speakers. The gap came from sounds and rhythms the systems had rarely been trained on, not from the words people chose.
move: A tool learns the voices it was fed and stumbles on the rest.
ask: Which tool I rely on was built for people unlike the ones I serve?
trap: About equal, since a machine has no prejudice about voices.
reference: Koenecke, Nam, Lake, Nudell, Quartey, Mengesha, Toups, Rickford, Jurafsky & Goel, Racial disparities in automated speech recognition, PNAS 117(14), 2020
